title: India Cine Hub Streamlines Filming Permissions, Boosts India’s Global Production Appeal
subtitle: India Cine Hub Brings Multiple Filming Clearances Under a Single Digital Platform: Panel at 57th IFFI
content:
Goa, 22 November 2026
India’s growing potential as a global filming and production destination came into focus at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), as policymakers and industry leaders discussed opportunities to strengthen the country’s position in the international filmmaking landscape.
The panel discussion, titled ‘
Filming Made Easy: India’s Rise as a Global Filming and Production Hub’
, featured Shri Prithul Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; Ms Grainne Brundson, Chief Operating Officer, Screen Australia; and veteran actor, director and producer Shri Anupam Kher.
The discussion explored how India Cine Hub (ICH), the single-window digital platform spearheaded by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting and operated by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), is facilitating filmmaking in India. Film critic and journalist Rajeev Masand moderated the session.
Opening the discussion, Shri Kumar said that the integration of State governments into the India Cine Hub portal marked a significant step towards simplifying filming permissions. Filmmakers can now use a common application form to seek clearances from multiple authorities, including municipal bodies, traffic departments, Indian Railways and the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), through a single digital interface.
He added that around 32 services have been mapped onto the platform. Applicants can track the progress of their applications through a dashboard, while payments, wherever required, are facilitated through secure payment links. Efforts are also underway to integrate drone-related permissions available through the Digital Sky platform.
Highlighting the growing ease of filming in India, Shri Kumar noted that international film shooting permissions, which have a stipulated processing period of 28 days, have taken an average of just 18 days since 2015. He also cited Madhya Pradesh’s deemed-approval provision, under which applications are treated as approved if no decision is communicated within 15 days.
Reflecting India's growing appeal as a filming and co-production destination, Shri Kumar noted that the number of international productions approaching India for such opportunities has risen from 25–30 to 100–200 annually. He encouraged production professionals and service providers to register on the portal, enabling filmmakers from across the world to discover and access India's production resources.
Speaking about opportunities for India-Australia collaboration, Ms Brundson said India's diverse filming locations, filmmaking talent and strong emotional connect with audiences made it an attractive destination for international partnerships. She highlighted the growing popularity of Indian cinema in Australia, observing that more people watched an Indian film than an Australian film in the country last year. The growing Indian-origin population and strong cultural, educational, sporting and business links between the two countries, she said, offered significant opportunities for collaborative storytelling.
Underlining the importance of government support for filmmaking, Ms Brundson said, “Every film is a start-up and a miracle. It begins with a dream or an idea and takes dedication, passion and the support of others to bring it to life.”
She added that successful co-productions go beyond financial collaboration and risk-sharing, creating opportunities for creative exchange. She highlighted the potential for Indian and Australian filmmakers to learn from each other’s storytelling traditions and explore shared experiences, including diaspora narratives, to create stories that resonate with audiences in both countries.
Appreciating the government of India's initiative to establish the India Cine Hub platform, Shri Anupam Kher said that the process of obtaining filming permissions had improved considerably. He observed that India's diverse landscapes, food, costumes and cultural settings offered filmmakers an extraordinary range of creative possibilities. Emphasising that cinema transcends geographical boundaries, he said, “Emotions don't have any different nationalities. The only thing that you need is the possibility of shooting.”
Shri Kher also noted that the single-window system benefits not only established producers but also newcomers, writers, production professionals and aspiring directors. He cautioned against the emergence of middlemen who could exploit filmmakers under the pretext of facilitating permissions.
The discussion brought into focus the growing opportunities for India to emerge as a preferred destination for international film productions, supported by streamlined permissions, diverse locations and opportunities for creative collaboration. In keeping with IFFI's role as a platform for global cinematic exchange, the session highlighted how stronger industry partnerships and an enabling filmmaking ecosystem can open new avenues for Indian cinema on the world stage.

title: North-East Cinema Brings Stories of Cultural Heritage, Identity and Social Realities to 57th IFFI
subtitle: Directors Aimee Baruah and Duyu Tabyo highlight cinema's role in preserving indigenous heritage, languages and untold stories of Northeast India
content:
Goa, 22 November 2026
From a traditional handloom weaving community in Assam striving to preserve its cultural heritage to a grieving father's psychological journey in the mountains of Arunachal Pradesh, two films from Northeast India bring distinct stories of identity, resilience and human emotions to the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI).
Red Carpet, an Assamese documentary featured in the Indian Panorama Non-Feature section while Urum is part of the Indian Panorama Feature Film category.
The films, Red Carpet (Assamese), directed by Aimee Baruah, and Urum, directed by Duyu Tabyo, were highlighted at a press conference held today in Goa, where the directors shared insights into their films and filmmaking journeys.
Red Carpet explores the traditional handloom weaving heritage of the Karbi community in Karbi Anglong, Assam, where a centuries-old craft faces the challenges of modernization and changing lifestyles. The documentary follows a traditional weaver's journey from the village of Donkamokam to the red carpet of Cannes, tracing how a handmade fabric became a symbol of cultural identity, pride and hope.
Sharing her perspective on the film, director Aimee Baruah, an award-winning Indian actress, producer and filmmaker pursuing her PhD, spoke about the journey of taking a traditional handwoven fabric from a small village in Assam to the prestigious red carpet of Cannes.
She highlighted the craftsmanship of local weavers and the cultural identity embodied in their traditional textiles, noting that the international recognition of the attire brought greater visibility to the region's indigenous heritage.
Emphasising the need to preserve traditional weaving practices, she urged the younger generation to take pride in their language, culture and traditions and carry this heritage forward.
The second film, Urum, directed by Duyu Tabyo, explores grief, memory and indigenous beliefs through the story of a father struggling to come to terms with the tragic loss of his young daughter in a remote mountain community of Arunachal Pradesh. As he grapples with guilt and haunting visions, the film follows his search for closure amid buried truths, trauma and the unseen forces shaping the lives of his people.
Director Duyu Tabyo, an independent writer-director and cultural practitioner from Arunachal Pradesh, whose work explores indigenous identity, memory and social realities, recalled an incident he witnessed during his childhood in Ziro, Arunachal Pradesh, involving a father struggling with the loss of his daughter. The memory stayed with him for years and eventually became the foundation of the film. He said that through the film, he sought to explore the psychological and emotional state of a grieving father rather than convey a particular moral message. Tabyo also expressed his gratitude to IFFI, describing his film's selection at IFFI as a significant recognition for Arunachal Pradesh's emerging film industry, expressing hope that it would encourage more young filmmakers from the state to tell their stories.
Emphasising the importance of linguistic and cultural preservation, Tabyo said that making the film in the indigenous Nishi language was a conscious decision to preserve its authenticity and bring greater visibility to the language. He noted that younger generations are increasingly losing touch with their indigenous languages and described the film as an effort to preserve the linguistic heritage of the Nishi community.
Speaking about the growing potential of cinema from Northeast India, Tabyo observed that the region remains an unexplored cinematic landscape with much to offer to the world. He noted the growing interest of mainstream filmmakers and production houses in the region, and emphasised that cinema can serve as a powerful medium for social awareness and change, beyond entertainment. He further highlighted the importance of documenting indigenous stories, languages and ways of life, saying that such efforts could help younger generations reconnect with their roots and appreciate the richness of their cultural identity.
The two films bring distinct narratives from Northeast India to the national cinematic platform, reflecting the region's diverse cultural experiences, indigenous traditions and contemporary realities. Their inclusion at the 57th International Film Festival of India adds to the cinematic diversity that characterises this year’s festival.

title: 'People Leaving Prison Deserve a Second Chance to Rebuild Their Lives': Director Nikita Grushin on 'New Home' at 57th IFFI
subtitle: Cinema Can Strengthen India-Russia Ties Through Cultural Understanding and Collaboration: Director Nikita Grushin
content:
Goa, 22 November 2026
People returning to society after spending years in prison often face an overlooked struggle to rebuild their lives and overcome the burden of their past, said Russian filmmaker Shri Nikita Grushin, director of
New Home
, at a press conference during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. The 101-minute Russian-language feature, making its World Premiere at IFFI 2026, is part of the special showcase celebrating Russia as the Partner Country at the festival.
Explaining the inspiration behind his film, Mr. Grushin said his interactions with people undergoing rehabilitation after prolonged imprisonment made him aware of the difficulties they face in reintegrating into society. He felt that these experiences received insufficient attention and wanted to bring their stories to a wider audience through his first internationally presented feature film. The film explores the struggles of both men and women seeking to rebuild their lives and find meaning after incarceration.
Written and directed by Mr. Grushin,
New Home
(
Novyy Dom
) follows Anna, a woman released from prison after seven years, with no money, family or clear direction in life. With assistance from social services, she finds employment, accommodation and a support group, where she meets Roman. As she gradually attempts to rebuild her life with his support, Anna must confront her past and inner struggles before making a difficult choice that could determine her future. The film explores themes of guilt, forgiveness, rehabilitation and the possibility of a second chance.
Speaking about the development of the central character, Mr. Grushin clarified that Anna was not modelled on any particular individual. Instead, he drew inspiration from conversations with several people who had experienced similar circumstances and were attempting to rebuild their lives. These real-life observations formed the foundation of the narrative, which he developed through his own writing and creative interpretation.
Reflecting on the film's central message, the director observed that the challenges faced by people leaving prison are not confined to any one country or society. Even after completing their sentences, many continue to carry a deep sense of guilt that influences their decisions and prevents them from moving forward. Through Anna's journey, he sought to explore how individuals confront this emotional burden and find the courage to begin again.
Cinematographer Ms. Ekaterina Smolina, who joined the director at the press conference, spoke about their creative partnership. Recalling their association since film school, she said they had previously collaborated on three short films. Their longstanding friendship and familiarity with each other's working styles helped establish a natural understanding on set, making the creative process both comfortable and rewarding.
Asked about the challenges faced by women entering cinematography, Ms. Smolina recalled that she too had initially experienced fear and uncertainty. However, she gradually overcame these apprehensions and encouraged aspiring women cinematographers to approach the profession with confidence and determination rather than allowing their initial fears to hold them back.
Speaking about opportunities for greater collaboration between Indian and Russian cinema, Mr. Grushin recalled the longstanding cinematic relationship between the two countries. Indian films, he observed, had enjoyed immense popularity in the Soviet Union and continued to occupy a special place in the hearts of Russian audiences.
Mr. Grushin expressed optimism about the potential for future Indo-Russian cinematic partnerships, emphasising that collaboration should extend beyond financial investment and technological exchange. Cultural engagement and stories highlighting the connections between the peoples of both countries, he said, could provide a meaningful foundation for stronger creative partnerships.
Through Anna's journey,
New Home
brings into focus a human experience that transcends national and cultural boundaries: the search for dignity, acceptance and a chance to begin again. In keeping with IFFI 2026's theme,
Stories Without Borders
, the film underscores cinema's ability to bring diverse realities closer, foster empathy and connect audiences through shared human experiences. Its presentation as part of Russia's Partner Country showcase also reflects the festival's role in strengthening cultural understanding and encouraging creative exchanges between India and the world.
The press conference was moderated by Shri Kiran Murali.

content:
Goa, 22 November 2026
The National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and Sony Pictures Networks India (SPNI) today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), Goa, to launch the
WAVES Bazaar × SPNI Content Creator Submission Initiative
.
The initiative will provide writers, creators and production houses across India an opportunity to pitch original fiction and non-fiction concepts to SPNI in Hindi, English, Tamil, Telugu and Bangla.
Submissions are invited across formats, including fiction series, premium TV+ content, reality shows, game and competition formats, talent-based programmes and other unscripted concepts. Selected applicants will be invited to pitch their concepts to SPNI for consideration and potential development.
Under the aegis of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, WAVES Bazaar, NFDC’s industry platform, connects creative talent with stakeholders across India's media and entertainment ecosystem. The collaboration aims to expand opportunities for original storytelling, particularly from regional markets, and bring diverse voices and perspectives to wider audiences.

It brings together stories, cultures and creative voices from across the world. The diversity of films and voices is what makes this edition special. The theme, Stories Without Borders, captures the spirit of cinema beautifully.”
Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director, NFDC said, “WAVES Bazaar continues to build meaningful connections between creative talent and the industry. This collaboration with Sony Pictures Networks India opens up new avenues for writers, creators and production houses to present original concepts across languages and formats.”
Gaurav Banerjee, Managing Director and CEO, Sony Pictures Networks India, said, “There is immense creative talent across the country, with ideas that may not always find their way to established platforms. Our partnership with NFDC through WAVES Bazaar is a step towards creating more avenues for writers and creators to bring their original concepts to us across languages and formats. We look forward to discovering fresh perspectives and compelling ideas for audiences.”

title: Chintan Shivir Deliberations will accelerate progress towards attaining Prime Minister’s Vision for Empowered Shram Shakti and Viksit Bharat: Union Minister  Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
subtitle:
Practical Insights from States and UTs Will Drive Effective Ground-Level Implementation of Labour Codes: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya

Strong Centre–State Coordination and Proactive Grievance Resolution Vital to Realise Vision of Dignity and Opportunity for Every Worker: MoS Sushri Shobha Karandlaje

Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Unveils NCS ONE Portal, e-Shram Livelihood Profile Module and Two Key Publications

Eight Career Lounges across the Country Virtually Launched by Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya

Two-Day Chintan Shivir of Labour, Employment & Industry Ministers of States/UTs Concludes in Gandhinagar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 NOV 2026 4:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, launched a diverse range of initiatives aimed at strengthening India’s labour and employment ecosystem on the second day of the two-day Chintan Shivir of Labour and Employment Ministers of States & Union Territories at Gandhinagar, Gujarat. Organised by the Ministry of Labour & Employment (MoLE), Government of India, on 21–22 November 2026, the conclave saw the participation of Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), alongside Labour and Employment Ministers and senior officials from States & Union Territories.
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya formally launched the National Career Service (NCS) ONE Portal with new features including the Voice Bot, Chat Bot, and Occupational Shortage Index (OSI), along with the e-Shram Livelihood Profile Module.
The National Career Service (NCS) Open Network for Employment (ONE) portal links job seeker apps, employer apps, state employment portals, private job platforms and campuses, while the Occupational Shortage Index (OSI) is a data-driven tool to assess labour market demand and supply gaps. The OSI will help jobseekers with informed career choices, employers in identifying shortage and plan recruitments, education & training institutions to align skilling, reskilling and upskilling with industry demand and policymakers with targeted employment and skilling interventions.
The e-Shram Livelihood Profile  tracks a worker's livelihood information alongside five essential social security protections (Panch Suraksha): food security, health protection, life insurance, accident and disability protection, and pension security.
In a significant expansion of the Ministry’s Career Lounges initiative, the Union Minister virtually launched eight Career Lounges at Jaipur, Ludhiana, Bhubaneswar, Kanpur, Bengaluru, Varanasi, Hyderabad, and Guwahati. Career Lounges are being established as a strategic extension of Model Career Centres (MCCs) under the National Career Service (NCS) framework, with 200 centres to be set up in employment exchanges, universities and educational institutions, particularly in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, in collaboration with industry partners. The Career Lounges will provide career guidance, skill and aptitude assessments, mentoring, employability training, industry interactions, internships, apprenticeships and placement support. They will also provide exposure to international employment opportunities, global labour market trends, international skill requirements and occupational standards, including language and cross-cultural preparedness, thereby enhancing the global employability of India's youth and connecting them with emerging opportunities in domestic and international labour markets.
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya also unveiled two publications at the event, namely the Addendum to the National Classification of Occupations (NCO-2015) and Compilation of Existing and Emerging Green Occupations.
Delivering his closing remarks, Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya observed that the two-day Chintan Shivir brought forward a wide range of practical insights, field experiences, and policy perspectives from States and Union Territories. He noted that acting decisively on these deliberations in alignment with the Prime Minister’s vision will guide the nation forward along the path to Viksit Bharat, while empowering India’s Shram Shakti.
Dr. Mandaviya further stated that the suggestions and learnings exchanged during the conclave will help safeguard and strengthen the interests of workers while supporting more effective ground-level implementation of the Labour Codes. Underscoring the importance of sustained Centre–State partnership, he emphasized that coordinated efforts and shared resolve will help build a responsive, inclusive, and future-ready labour and employment ecosystem across the country.
Summing up the deliberations of the Chintan Shivir, Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment and MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, congratulated all participants and appreciated their active engagement in sharing best practices and suggestions. Stressing strong Centre–State coordination and international mobility for youth, she emphasized training lawyers and consultants for proactive grievance resolution before cases even reach court. Noting that participating stakeholders represent the interests of the workforce, she highlighted collective responsibility towards achieving the Prime Minister's vision of dignity and opportunity for every worker. Commending active State participation and encouraging time-bound outcomes from the breakaway sessions, she urged the compiling of takeaways so insights can be acted upon and institutionalized.
Day 2 of the Chintan Shivir included sessions on the Labour & Employment Stack and Career Lounges for International Labour Mobility. These sessions featured presentations by officials. Participating states also shared best-practice videos. Across both days, thematic plenary sessions covered Labour Codes implementation, employment initiatives and Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) reforms, Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) reforms, and social security for unorganized workers along with labour statistics. Parallel Breakaway Sessions for State/UT field officials focused on MSME engagement, field-level initiatives, and trust-based electronic compliances. They also covered Central and State grievance redressal mechanisms, the National Classification of Occupations (NCO), and the District Employment Profile framework. Insights and recommendations from both days' Breakaway Sessions were then discussed and deliberated upon.
The Chintan Shivir marked one year since the coming into effect of the Labour Codes on 21 November 2025, with States and Union Territories sharing their best practices and V. V. Giri National Labour Institute (VVGNLI), Noida, and Gujarat National Law University (GNLU), Gandhinagar, serving as Knowledge Partners for the two-day conclave. Through focused deliberations and shared resolve, the event reinforced cooperative federalism to strengthen Centre–State coordination, enhance digital service delivery, and advance the effective implementation of labour reforms and social security initiatives towards the vision of
Viksit Bharat
.

title: India’s Healthcare Research Focus Shifting to Prevention Through Futuristic Strategies at molecular and genetic levels: Dr Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Preventive healthcare assumes importance as metabolic disorders increasingly affect younger populations, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

India advances disease research to molecular and genetic levels, opening new frontiers in precision medicine and early interventions: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Genome sequencing of 10,000 Indians across 84 populations strengthens understanding of India's genetic diversity and disease susceptibility, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Over 50 lakh adolescent girls vaccinated against HPV as India expands preventive healthcare, indigenous medical research and genetic therapies: Dr. Jitendra Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 NOV 2026 3:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh said India is moving towards a futuristic healthcare approach with research focus shifting to prevention through futuristic strategies that places greater emphasis on prevention, early detection and advanced research at molecular and genetic levels, as metabolic disorders and lifestyle-related diseases increasingly affect younger populations. Emphasising that protecting the health of India's young population is critical to the nation's future, he said healthcare is evolving beyond conventional treatment approaches towards scientific interventions, preventive strategies and more precise disease management, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Dr. Jitendra Singh was speaking at THE WEEK Health Summit 2026 in New Delhi, where he delivered the Chief Guest Address on *Healthcare Initiatives of the Union Government* and participated in an interaction with healthcare professionals, researchers and industry representatives. The summit brought together prominent healthcare experts, including Dr. Nikhil Tandon, Director, AIIMS New Delhi; Sharad Aggarwal, Director, FSSAI; Dr. Andrei Kozik, Deputy Head–India, International Committee of the Red Cross, besides senior doctors, medical researchers and representatives of leading healthcare institutions.
Addressing the growing burden of metabolic disorders, Dr. Jitendra Singh said diabetes, obesity, hypertension and cardiovascular diseases are increasingly affecting younger people, making preventive healthcare and early detection imperative. He said changing dietary patterns, declining physical activity and the spread of lifestyle-related health risks across urban and rural India have made the challenge more widespread. Prevention, he said, cannot be left to medical professionals alone and requires collective societal participation and greater awareness.
The Minister said India is progressing towards futuristic healthcare strategies through research at molecular and genetic levels, with scientific efforts increasingly extending beyond conventional treatment to explore deeper mechanisms of diseases and potential interventions. He said advances in biotechnology, genetic research and molecular science are strengthening India's ability to address complex health conditions and develop more precise and effective approaches to disease management.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India has witnessed a major transformation in its healthcare and scientific capabilities and is emerging as an important global contributor in preventive healthcare and vaccine development. Referring to India's indigenous DNA vaccine developed during the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent advances in vaccine research, he cited the HPV vaccination initiative under which more than 50 lakh adolescent girls have already been vaccinated, contributing to efforts towards cervical cancer prevention.
Highlighting India's advances in genomics, the Minister said genome sequencing of 10,000 Indian individuals belonging to 84 different populations has been undertaken, reflecting the country's unique genetic diversity. With more than 400 genetic traits across different populations, India's genetic landscape offers significant opportunities for research into disease susceptibility, healthcare risks and the development of targeted medical interventions.
Referring to the emerging field of precision medicine, Dr. Jitendra Singh said healthcare is increasingly moving towards personalised treatment approaches based on an individual's genetic profile, lifestyle, environment and other factors. He explained that the same disease may require different treatment approaches for different individuals, making precision medicine an important frontier. He also referred to ongoing research into biomarkers among women with gestational diabetes to identify those at greater risk of developing Type 2 diabetes in later life and enable more targeted follow-up.
The Minister said the Government and ICMR are working towards expanding the coverage of rare genetic diseases to improve access to diagnosis and treatment and make therapies more accessible and affordable. He said rare diseases often impose a disproportionate burden on affected individuals and their families, owing to diagnostic difficulties, high treatment costs and limited availability of medicines, requiring sustained scientific and institutional efforts.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India is also making significant progress in indigenous medical research, including the development of new antibiotics and advancements in genetic therapies. Referring to gene therapy research for haemophilia undertaken by Christian Medical College, Vellore, and published in the New England Journal of Medicine, he said Indian researchers are increasingly developing advanced medical solutions with potential applications beyond the country, reflecting India's growing research capabilities.
Referring to healthcare infrastructure and disease management, the Minister said the expansion of dialysis facilities across district hospitals has improved access to treatment for kidney patients, while research is also advancing towards detection of kidney disease at earlier stages, even before symptoms become apparent. He emphasised that prevention and effective management of diabetes and hypertension remain essential to protecting vital organs and reducing the long-term burden of chronic diseases.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said greater collaboration between government institutions, research organisations, healthcare professionals and private-sector partners is essential to accelerate medical research and translate scientific discoveries into practical healthcare solutions. He said increased participation of private players has opened new avenues for research, innovation and development, while also stressing the need to encourage philanthropy to strengthen support for medical research.
Addressing young people, the Minister cautioned against health-related misinformation, unverified nutrition advice and the unsupervised use of medicines for cosmetic purposes. He advised young people to seek guidance from qualified medical professionals and rely on authenticated scientific information, stressing that informed decisions and responsible health practices are crucial for a healthier society.
India's expanding capabilities in preventive healthcare, molecular and genetic research, genomics, biotechnology and indigenous medical innovation are paving the way for a more futuristic and precision-driven healthcare ecosystem, with scientific advancement and early intervention playing an increasingly important role in addressing emerging health challenges.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi  participates in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh
subtitle:
21st-century India can progress only by honouring skills; Therefore, over the past years, our government has taken a series of steps guided by the spirit of 'Shrameva Jayate': PM

When you learn a skill, you do not merely work on machines; you make people's lives easier and strengthen the nation's capabilities: PM

Today, India is advancing towards becoming the skill capital of the world: PM

I urge every young person in the country; the entire sky lies open before you today, dream big, hone your skills, and dedicate all your energy to fulfilling your dreams: PM
ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 NOV 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister expressed happiness that Lucknow was chosen to host such a major skill development event, noting that as a Member of Parliament from Uttar Pradesh, it is a matter of pride for him as well.
Observing that the graduating youth have crossed an important milestone in their lives and are now set to join the process of nation-building directly, the Prime Minister emphasized that the skills and craftsmanship they acquired at ITIs serve as a major driving force for a Viksit Bharat. He added that any nation progresses capably in this very manner through the skills of its youth. Highlighting India's long-standing respect for craftsmanship, he cited Lucknow's Chikankari, fine muslin, Banaras and Kanjeevaram silk, Kashmir Pashmina, cotton textiles, Kalamkari, steel for the world's finest swords, and bronze and Panchdhatu idols as hundreds of traditional crafts that once formed society's foundational pillars. “For a long time, India's identity in the world has been through such skills,” observed PM Modi.
Explaining that India's earlier social system was structured around skills, the Prime Minister shared the example of Gujarat's Vasavaya tradition, under which skilled artisans who sustained village life settled wherever a new village was established. “These were such skilled people without whom it was difficult even to imagine village life,” remarked Shri Modi.
Pointing out that while such a system existed across every region of India since ancient times, it gradually lost importance, the Prime Minister recalled an exercise he assigned to officers as Chief Minister of Gujarat to list every task and service a person needs from waking up to sleeping and from birth to death, which yielded around one thousand essential skills that kept society moving. “I asked the officers to focus on this very thing, and then a modern ecosystem of skill development was created there in Gujarat,” noted PM Modi.
Attributing the decline of India's skill ecosystem to the colonial education system which reduced a skill-based society to producing paper clerks while the British advanced their own industry and manufacturing, the Prime Minister observed that clerical jobs came to be revered even after independence while skilled craftspeople were subjected to an inferiority complex and began shying away from their trades. “Our country has had to suffer a huge loss due to this mentality of slavery,” asserted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the government's successive initiatives driven by the spirit of Shrameva Jayate, including extending the tradition of convocations beyond college and university degree holders to ITI skill certificate recipients and placing strong emphasis on skill development in the new National Education Policy, the Prime Minister underscored the importance of honoring craftsmanship. “The India of the 21st century can move forward only by giving respect to skill,” asserted PM Modi.
Addressing widespread discussions and anxieties about Artificial Intelligence taking away jobs in the modern era, the Prime Minister recalled how during the COVID pandemic, when everyone felt helpless, it was skilled workers who managed critical operations and kept things running. “Understand this point of mine very well: whoever has skill, no one can take away their employment,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing that learning a craft goes beyond operating machines to making people's lives easier while strengthening national capability and manufacturing capacity, the Prime Minister highlighted the unprecedented focus on ITIs since 2014, noting that nearly 5,000 new ITIs have been built in a single decade. “The number of those studying in ITIs has also increased by more than 5 lakh, and in this too, the number of girls has become more than two and a half times,” noted PM Modi.
Highlighting the focus on training, quality, faculty, and infrastructure in ITIs, which had previously lagged behind with outdated trades, the Prime Minister noted that over 30 new-age trades have now been introduced, including Aeronautical Structure, Artificial Intelligence Assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, Drone Technician, Green Hydrogen Technician, Industrial Robotics, Electric Vehicles, Animation and Special Effects, and Semiconductor Technician, designed for both Indian and global needs alongside India's ongoing trade agreements and FTA discussions. “All of this is being done for you, the youth; new opportunities are being created for your future,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing efforts to modernize ITI curricula and machinery, train instructors in new technologies, and build direct links between training and industry, the Prime Minister highlighted the investment of 60,000 crore rupees under the PM-SETU scheme.“Our youth are going to benefit immensely from this,” affirmed PM Modi.
Noting that India's rapid development is generating vast employment opportunities for skilled workers, the Prime Minister pointed to the 50 crore people lifted out of poverty over the past 12 to 13 years through government facilities that instilled confidence. Citing mega campaigns such as building 4 crore houses for the poor, laying water pipelines, and delivering first-time electricity lines where electricians, carpenters, and other skilled youth found work, he underlined the scale of job creation. “In this mega campaign, lakhs and lakhs of new opportunities were also created for skilled workers in the country,” observed Shri Modi.
Highlighting rising skill demand across emerging sectors, the Prime Minister cited the disruption in gas supplies during the West Asia conflict a few months ago, when the government targeted at least one lakh PNG connections per day and review meetings repeatedly flagged a shortage of plumbers delaying targets, while pointing to huge skilled manpower needs in solar power and the burgeoning sports economy spanning sports equipment manufacturing and fitness. “If you are skilled, you have that many more opportunities to get employment,” asserted PM Modi.
Announcing that India is advancing toward becoming the skill capital of the world, the Prime Minister shared good news for youth and Uttar Pradesh that India will host the WorldSkills Asia competition in 2027 in Greater Noida, welcoming youth from numerous countries. “I extend advance best wishes to UP for this as well,” remarked Shri Modi.
Praising Uttar Pradesh for accelerating national development, the Prime Minister credited the present government under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for transforming the state into an expressway state with multiple international airports, major universities, flourishing tourism, large mobile manufacturing plants, an upcoming chip factory, and manufacturing of BrahMos, which shook the enemy in Operation Sindoor. “Because of all these development works happening in UP, new opportunities are being created for you youth,” observed PM Modi.
Recalling a recent interaction during a factory inauguration in his parliamentary constituency of Banaras where a young woman told him she now returns home comfortably even at 11 PM, the Prime Minister credited the current government under Yogi Adityanath for creating an environment of security, asserting that the sense of security and confidence of prosperity will build a Viksit Bharat, and extended his heartiest best wishes to all youth. “The entire sky is before you at this time; dream big, develop your skills, and put your full strength into fulfilling your dreams,” asserted Shri Modi.

title: Partnerships With Universities, Rural Development Institutes, Other Reputed Institutions Could Help Advance Training, Capacity Building, Rehabilitation, Livelihood Opportunities And Social Inclusion For Individuals Affected By Substance Use, Transgender Persons, Senior Citizens And Persons Vulnerable To Beggary: Dr Virendra Kumar
subtitle: NISD Exchanges 23 MoUs with Universities and Institutions Across India to Strengthen Social Defence Initiatives
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 NOV 2026 7:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr Virendra Kumar has said that partnerships with universities, rural development institutes and other reputed institutions could help advance training, capacity building, rehabilitation, livelihood opportunities and social inclusion for individuals affected by substance use, transgender persons, senior citizens and persons vulnerable to beggary.
Addressing the gathering at MoU exchange ceremony of National Institute Of Social Defence (NISD) at its campus in the National Capital here, Dr Kumar said the initiative would strengthen efforts towards enabling vulnerable individuals to lead dignified, self-reliant lives and contribute meaningfully to society.
The National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, exchanged MoUs with 23 universities, organizations and the institutions across the country as part of wider collaboration to strengthen the work of NISD through institutional partnerships.
Out of these, 15 institutions participated in person and 8 institutions joined virtually. With this, NISD’s institutional partnerships have increased to 30, building upon the 7 MoUs signed earlier with universities and organisations.
Describing the initiative as significant and historic, Dr Kumar underscored the need to have regular dialogue and consultations, review of initiatives and sharing of best practices among institutions would help extend effective interventions across different States and regions.
Dr Kumar said that sustained awareness activities, including periodic anti-drug pledges in educational institutions, could help create a wider chain of awareness and collective action towards a drug-free India.
The Minister urged NISD and its partner institutions to explore regular coordination, monitoring and short-term training programmes within campuses to strengthen collaborative efforts in drug abuse prevention.
Union Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, highlighted the important role of educational institutions in preventing drug abuse among young people. He enjoined upon institutions to organise regular anti-drug awareness activities and pledges, enabling students to carry the message of drug prevention from their campuses to families, peers and communities.
Shri Pant also stressed the need for regular coordination, monitoring and mutually beneficial training programmes between NISD and partner institutions.
The Secretary said that sustained awareness activities, including periodic anti-drug pledges in educational institutions, could help create a wider chain of awareness and collective action towards a drug-free India. He urged NISD and its partner institutions to explore regular coordination, monitoring and short-term training programmes within campuses to strengthen collaborative efforts in drug abuse prevention.
The ceremony was graced by Dr Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Union Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Dr Sandeep Rewaji Rathod, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment and Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, Director, NISD, New Delhi, and other senior officers, officials of NISD and the Ministry.
The 23 institutions include State Institute of Rural Development, Ranchi, Jharkhand; State Institute of Rural Development, Meghalaya; State Institute of Rural Development (SIRD), Manipur; Telangana Institute of Rural Development (TGIRD), Telangana; Central University of Andhra Pradesh; Central University of Karnataka; Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Lucknow; National Law University, Jodhpur; Shri Vishwakarma Skill University, Haryana; and Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University, Karnataka.
In addition, CHRIST University, Bengaluru; Yenepoya (Deemed to be University), Karnataka; Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi; Aligarh Muslim University, Uttar Pradesh; Indian Adult Education Association, New Delhi; Andhra Pradesh State Institute of Panchayat Raj & Rural Development; AIIMS Jodhpur, Rajasthan; Administrative Training Centre, Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA), Puducherry; Kerala Institute of Local Administration (KILA), Kerala; Maharashtra National Law University, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar; Chanakya National Law University, Patna; Mahatma Gandhi Central University, Bihar; and Maharashtra National Law University, Nagpur, are among other institutions who signed MoUs with NISD.
The scope of these MoUs covers Prevention Education, Research, Training and Capacity Building, Curriculum Development, and Outreach and Advocacy in the field of Social Defence, including Drug Abuse Prevention, Welfare of Senior Citizens, Transgender Welfare and Prevention of Beggary.
The partnerships are expected to facilitate institutional collaboration, knowledge exchange, training opportunities and the development of effective interventions across these areas.
On the occasion, the Union Minister administered
‘Senior Citizen’
and
‘Anti Drug’
Pledges to the participants, refreshing the sense of responsibility towards working for creating awareness among common masses, to uphold respect,  dignity and and to ensure healthcare and welfare of the senior citizens besides Drug Abuse Prevention and treatment and rehabilitation of the persons affected by the substance abuse.
The expanded network of institutional partnerships is expected to create a sustained framework for training, awareness generation, research and evidence-based interventions in the field of Social Defence.
Through collaboration with universities, public training institutions and specialised organisations across the country, NISD will further strengthen its efforts towards the welfare, rehabilitation, empowerment and social inclusion of vulnerable sections of society.
The initiative reinforces the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s commitment to strengthening institutional collaboration and advancing a socially secure, inclusive and empowered India.
Earlier, Dr Sandeep Rewaji Rathod, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, welcomed the dignitaries and senior representatives from the participating universities and organizations.
Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, Director, NISD, New Delhi, presented vote of thanks.
Ms Anushka Bhardwaj, Junior Consultant at NISD, conducted the proceedings

title: Fit India’s 99th Sundays on Cycle Celebrated Across 26,000 Locations to Mark Samvidhan Divas
subtitle:
Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Gujarat Dy CM Harsh Sanghavi Lead 99th Edition Celebrations at Dandi Kutir

100th Edition on 29 November to Celebrate the Olympic Movement in India
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:

content:
Gandhinagar, 22 November 2026: The 99th edition of Fit India Sundays on Cycle was celebrated across 26,000 locations nationwide on Sunday, with the theme of Samvidhan Divas, reinforcing the message of fitness, civic responsibility and collective participation in nation-building.
Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports and Labour & Employment, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghavi led the celebrations at Dandi Kutir and Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar, joining citizens, sportspersons and fitness enthusiasts in promoting an active and healthy lifestyle.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya said that a fit, healthy and drug-free youth population is essential to achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. He called upon citizens, particularly the youth, to make cycling a passion and an integral part of everyday life.
“Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we are working towards building a Viksit Bharat. The participation of people across 26,000 locations in the 99th edition of Sundays on Cycle makes this occasion special, particularly as we approach Samvidhan Divas on 26 November. Fitness should not be limited to a few hours or a particular day; it should become a part of our everyday lives,” Dr. Mandaviya said.
Dr. Mandaviya also said that cycling is not just a physical activity but a way to promote fitness and spread awareness about healthy living.
“Our youth must be conscious not only about their careers but also about their fitness and responsibility towards the nation,” he further said.
Dr. Mandaviya also called for making cycling a popular lifestyle choice, emphasising that greater public participation in cycling would help promote fitness and build a healthier society. He said that small individual efforts, when taken together, could bring about a larger transformation and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.
“The simple mantra for a fit India is that every citizen must become health-conscious. When our citizens are fit, our society will be healthy, and a healthy society is essential for building a prosperous nation. Let us all join hands, make fitness a priority and contribute to the journey towards Viksit Bharat,” he said.
100th Edition to Celebrate the Olympic Movement in India
Building on the growing nationwide participation, Dr. Mandaviya announced that the 100th edition of Sundays on Cycle, scheduled for 29 November 2026, will celebrate the Olympic Movement in India.
The milestone edition will reaffirm India's commitment to Olympic values and the promotion of sports and physical activity among citizens, particularly the youth.
Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghavi appreciated the growing nationwide participation in Sundays on Cycle and said that the initiative is inspiring citizens to adopt healthier lifestyles and make fitness a regular habit.

title: Harnessing Small Hydro Power
subtitle: Strengthening Energy Security for Sustainable Development
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 NOV 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Small hydropower uses the natural flow of rivers and canals to generate clean, reliable electricity. In India, projects with capacity up to 25 MW fall within this category. They suit hilly, remote areas where terrain limits larger projects and grid reach. India has an identified potential of 21,134 MW across 7,133 sites, of which about a quarter is harnessed. These projects need little land, cause minimal displacement and offer a long operational life. With sustained policy support, small hydropower can strengthen energy access across India's underserved regions.
Introduction
Hydropower, generated from the natural flow of water, is among the world's most reliable and established renewable energy sources. Amid India's evolving energy landscape, it plays a pivotal role in ensuring grid stability, energy security, and power system resilience. Hydropower provides firm, round-the-clock electricity alongside operational flexibility. As India accelerates its transition towards a cleaner energy mix, hydropower remains an important pillar of sustainable electricity generation.
Small Hydropower (SHP), comprising projects with installed capacity up to
25 MW
, offers significant opportunities for harnessing India's untapped water resources. With substantial potential across Himalayan states, the North Eastern region, and other parts of the country, small hydro projects can contribute meaningfully to India's renewable energy capacity. Recognising this potential, the Government of India has introduced various initiatives to promote small hydropower development, encourage investment, and harness untapped resources. These efforts aim to expand clean energy generation while improving electricity access in remote and geographically challenging regions.
Beyond electricity generation, small hydropower offers several developmental and economic benefits. Compared with large hydroelectric projects, these installations generally require smaller land areas and can have relatively limited environmental footprints. They can promote local investment, generate employment, strengthen regional infrastructure, and support economic activities in remote areas. By complementing other renewable energy sources and diversifying the country's energy portfolio, small hydropower can contribute to India's energy security and sustainable development objectives.
Did You Know?
In India, the primary distinction between
large and small hydropower projects
lies in their installed capacity and the respective ministerial jurisdiction. Small Hydropower Projects (SHP) are defined as those with an installed capacity of up to 25 MW and are administered by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). In contrast, large hydropower projects, with capacity exceeding 25 MW, fall under the purview of the Ministry of Power.
Government Initiatives for Small Hydropower Development
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is the nodal ministry responsible for promoting small hydro projects.
The Government of India has recently approved the
Small Hydro Power (SHP) Development Scheme
for FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31, with an outlay of
Rs.
2,584.60 crore
. The scheme aims to add approximately
1,500 MW
of small hydro capacity. It prioritises hilly, North-Eastern and border regions through financial assistance, project preparation support and technical capacity building.
The scheme outlines a set of targeted measures to support implementation, improve project viability, and ensure a steady pipeline of SHP projects across regions. It focuses on addressing key constraints related to financing, project readiness, and execution, particularly in challenging geographies. Together, these measures are intended to enable faster and more efficient deployment of SHP capacity.
Financial Support Structure:
Financial assistance to
North Eastern States & International Border Districts
of
Rs
3.6 crore per MW or 30% of project cost (whichever is lower)
, subject to a ceiling of
Rs
30 crore per project
.
Financial assistance to other locations of
@ Rs 2.4/1.78/2.054 crore per MW (depending on the size and location of the project) or 20% of project cost (whichever is lower)
, with a cap of
Rs
20 crore per project
.
Investment and Economic Impact:
The scheme is expected to attract
investments of around
Rs
15,000 crore
in the small hydro sector.
It will also promote the use of
indigenous plant and machinery
, contributing to the vision of
Atmanirbhar Bharat
while boosting local manufacturing and supply chains.
Pipeline Development and DPR Support:
To ensure long-term sector growth, the scheme provides support for the preparation of
Detailed Project Reports (DPRs)
for a minimum of
200 projects
. An allocation of
Rs 30
crore
has been made separately to assist central and state agencies in developing a strong future project pipeline.
Employment Generation:
The scheme is expected to generate approximately
51 lakh person-days of employment
during the construction phase. In addition, it will create sustained employment opportunities in the
operation and maintenance
of projects, particularly in rural and remote regions.
The approval of the SHP Development Scheme marks a significant step towards unlocking India’s untapped small hydro potential. By combining targeted financial support, infrastructure development, and sustainability, the scheme is set to strengthen clean energy capacity while driving inclusive growth in underserved regions.
Significance of Small Hydro Power for Sustainable Energy Development
Small hydro power plays
a vital role in advancing clean, reliable, and decentralised energy in India. Particularly suited for remote and hilly regions, these projects utilise locally available water resources to generate electricity close to consumption centres. This not only improves energy access but also reduces dependence on long transmission networks and enhances overall efficiency.
Decentralised and Efficient Power Supply:
Located near demand centres, these projects minimise transmission losses, improve voltage stability, and ensure reliable power in geographically challenging areas, including border and hilly regions.
Clean and Cost-Effective Energy Source:
Small hydro power generates electricity without fuel consumption or emissions, making it a sustainable and economically viable long-term solution.
Driver of Rural Development:
By improving electricity access in underserved areas, these projects support infrastructure development and act as a catalyst for local economic growth.
Employment and Livelihood Generation:
They create both direct and indirect employment opportunities during construction and operation, while also promoting small-scale industries and self-employment.
Environmentally Sustainable:
With minimal land requirement and negligible displacement, small hydro power projects have a low ecological footprint and limited social impact. Their long operational life further strengthens their sustainability.
SHP offers a balanced solution that combines energy security with sustainable development. By delivering reliable, round-the-clock power and strengthening grid resilience, especially in remote areas, they contribute significantly to inclusive growth. Their ability to integrate environmental sustainability with socio-economic benefits makes them a key component of India’s clean energy transition.
Small Hydro Power Potential and Prospects in India
SHP
is emerging as a vital and reliable component of India’s clean energy transition. It is particularly well-suited for hilly, remote, and difficult terrains where decentralised generation can deliver sustainable power, enhance energy access, and support local livelihoods.
India possesses a significant SHP potential of 21,134 MW across 7,133 identified sites. As of 30 September 2026, approximately 5,182 MW (around 25%) has already been harnessed, demonstrating steady progress. The remaining 15,952 MW represents a substantial opportunity for accelerated development through focused policy support and public-private collaboration.
The regional distribution of this potential further reflects India’s rich geographical diversity and offers unique strengths across the country. The Northern region has 8,030 MW of SHP potential, particularly across mountainous terrains. The North-Eastern region holds 2,995 MW, positioning it as a key frontier for expansion, especially in hilly regions and the North Eastern States. The list is followed by Southern region with 5,490 MW of SHP, supported by well-developed river systems and infrastructure. The Western region has a potential of 2,912 MW of SHP, while the Eastern region accounts for 1,707 MW
with strong potential in rural and tribal areas.
This distributed potential allows for a
balanced, region-specific strategy
. While the Northern and North-Eastern regions offer large untapped resources, the Southern and Western regions are better positioned for quicker implementation due to stronger infrastructure. With the recently approved Small Hydro Power Development Scheme, the Government of India is committed to harnessing this diverse potential through targeted incentives, simplified procedures, and enhanced financial support.
By adopting a focused yet inclusive approach, India is poised to unlock the full benefits of small hydropower, strengthening energy security, promoting inclusive growth, and advancing the nation’s goal of a sustainable and self-reliant energy future.
Northern region
The Northern region forms the backbone of India’s SHP landscape, driven by its mountainous terrain, perennial rivers, and favourable hydrology, making it particularly significant for development in hilly regions. States such as Himachal Pradesh (3,460 MW), Uttarakhand (1,664 MW), and Jammu & Kashmir (1,312 MW) dominate the region’s potential, with Ladakh (396 MW) adding strategic importance. Despite this strong resource base, utilisation levels remain moderate, indicating substantial untapped capacity.
Did You Know?
Run-of-the-river projects
generate electricity by using the natural flow of river water without building large dams. A portion of water is diverted through channels and pipes to run turbines and is then released back into the stream, ensuring minimal ecological disruption.
North-East region
The North-Eastern region represents a
high-potential growth frontier
, particularly critical for expanding renewable energy in
hilly regions and the North Eastern States
.
Arunachal Pradesh (2,065 MW) constitutes the largest share of the regional potential, followed by Meghalaya (230 MW), Assam (202 MW), Nagaland (182 MW), Mizoram (169 MW), Manipur (100 MW), and Tripura (47 MW).
SHP development in this region offers strong opportunities for decentralised and off-grid energy solutions, particularly in remote and tribal areas. It can significantly enhance energy access, promote local employment, and reduce reliance on conventional fuels. With targeted policy interventions, improved connectivity, and community-driven models, the North-Eastern region can emerge as a major engine of growth for India’s SHP sector
Southern region
The Southern region is a key contributor to SHP development, supported by strong infrastructure, established energy systems, and favourable river basins.
Karnataka leads with 3,726 MW
, accounting for nearly 68% of the regional potential, followed by Keralam    647 MW and Tamil Nadu 604 MW. The region has achieved relatively higher utilisation levels compared to others, reflecting efficient project execution and strong grid connectivity.
With its robust infrastructure base, the Southern region is well-positioned to scale further through optimisation of existing assets and integration with other clean energy sources. It will continue to play a stabilising role in India’s SHP expansion, complementing growth in hilly regions and the North Eastern States.
Eastern region
The Eastern region offers
moderate but strategically important SHP potential
, particularly for decentralised development in rural and tribal areas.
Bihar (527 MW), West Bengal (392 MW) and Odisha (286 MW) lead the region, followed by Sikkim (267 MW) and Jharkhand (228 MW). The region’s river systems and terrain provide favourable conditions for small-scale hydro projects.
Expanding SHP in this region can improve
local energy access, agricultural productivity, and rural livelihoods
, while supporting inclusive development. With targeted interventions, improved financing mechanisms, and decentralised deployment models, the Eastern region can complement national growth.
Western region
The Western region presents
unique opportunities for SHP development
, particularly through its extensive
irrigation and canal-based infrastructure
.
Chhattisgarh leads the region with 1,098.20 MW of potential, followed by Madhya Pradesh (820 MW) and Maharashtra (786 MW). Against a regional potential of 2,912 MW, installed capacity stands at 730 MW. Maharashtra and Gujarat record relatively higher utilisation, while others continue to offer scope for expansion.
The region’s focus on
canal-based and dam-toe projects
provides a cost-effective pathway for scaling SHP capacity. By leveraging existing infrastructure and promoting innovative deployment models, the Western region can strengthen decentralised renewable energy generation. Alongside advancements in
hilly regions and the North Eastern States
, it can play a critical role in ensuring a balanced and diversified SHP growth trajectory.
Did You Know?
SHP projects on canal falls or dam toe utilise the drop in water levels in irrigation canals or just below dams and barrages to generate electricity. Water is diverted to the powerhouse and returned to the main canal after power generation, making use of existing water infrastructure.
Conclusion
The Small Hydro Power Development Scheme (2026-31) marks a decisive policy intervention by the Government of India to harness the unique strengths of small hydropower in the country’s clean energy journey. With an outlay of
Rs
2,584.60 crore aimed at adding 1,500 MW of new capacity, the scheme prioritises reliable, decentralised power generation, especially in challenging terrains where other renewable sources face limitations.
Beyond capacity creation, the initiative is designed to deliver broader developmental outcomes. By combining targeted financial support, streamlined project preparation, and promotion of indigenous manufacturing, it will stimulate private investment, strengthen domestic supply chains, and generate meaningful employment opportunities in remote and rural regions. This integrated approach positions small hydropower as an effective tool for inclusive growth and regional equity.
As India advances towards greater energy self-reliance and a sustainable future, small hydro power offers a balanced solution that combines environmental responsibility with socio-economic progress. With this focused push, the Government of India is confident that the scheme will illuminate underserved areas, enhance grid resilience, and contribute meaningfully to building a cleaner, stronger, and more self-sufficient India.
